priority_blocker_addressed.claim: Production runtime must be real Socket.IO HTTP server, not RoomManager-only gate1 mirror; save/load, host loss, and crash resilience must be evidenced against that real server.
priority_blocker_addressed.finding: gate1/tools/core_loop_runner.ts constructs RoomManager in-process with zero WebSocket frames — not ACTUAL_PRODUCTION_RUNTIME. Beyond that gap, every socket.io event handler read request payload fields (e.g. `data.code.toUpperCase()`, `input.playerId`) with no null/shape checks. A single malformed event from any one client (host, player, or a stray/attacker connection) threw synchronously inside the socket.io callback and crashed the entire Node process for every room and every connected client — a real one-client denial-of-service, not a harness artifact.
priority_blocker_addressed.fix: Added apps/server/src/load/wp014ProductionGate.ts, which binds setupRealtime on an ephemeral HTTP server and drives room.create/join/select_song/roles/calibration/countdown/game.input/end/rematch/host_reconnect/host-loss/player-reconnect over real socket.io-client WebSockets end to end. Hardened apps/server/src/realtime/socket.ts by monkey-patching socket.on immediately on connection so every handler registered afterward is wrapped in try/catch: a thrown error is logged and reported to the offending client via a `room.error` event instead of crashing the process. Added a real Web Audio unit test (apps/web/src/lib/hostAudio.test.ts) driving playClick/resumeAudioContext/startHostMetronome against a spec-shaped AudioContext double.
priority_blocker_addressed.real_defect_found_and_fixed: Unguarded field access in socket.io handlers (`room.select_song`, `game.input`, `room.join`, etc.) let one malformed client payload crash the whole server process for all rooms/players. Verified before/after: the harness's crash_recovery_malformed_input step sends exactly these malformed payloads on a throwaway connection and then proves the server still answers a legitimate room.create on the same connection afterward.

defects.S1_fixed_detail: Unwrapped socket.io event handlers crashed the entire Node process on a single malformed client payload (null/wrong-typed fields on room.select_song, game.input, room.join, etc.) — fixed by wrapping every handler registered via socket.on in a try/catch that reports room.error to the offending client instead of taking the whole server down.
